component.name: velocity
component.title: Velocity
component.description: Render a Velocity template with the data of the message and use the text it writes as the new message body.
component.label: transformation

allowContextMapAll.description: Sets whether the context map should allow access to all details. By default only the message body and headers can be accessed. This option can be enabled for full access to the current Exchange and CamelContext. Doing so impose a potential security risk as this opens access to the full power of CamelContext API.

allowTemplateFromHeader.description: Whether the producer reads the CamelVelocityResourceUri, CamelVelocityTemplate, CamelVelocityContext and CamelVelocitySupplementalContext headers. If false, the producer ignores all four headers. Enable it only when the route sets these headers, not a message sender.

contentCache.description: Sets whether to use resource content cache or not

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

velocityEngine.label: advanced
velocityEngine.description: To use a custom org.apache.velocity.app.VelocityEngine for all endpoints of the component. If not set, each endpoint creates its own engine, which loads the templates that a template includes with #parse or #include from the file system and the classpath, and applies the loaderCache and propertiesFile options.

CamelVelocityResourceUri.description: The URI of a template that the producer renders in place of the template of resourceUri, in the same form as resourceUri. Only used when allowTemplateFromHeader is true. The producer removes the header and hands the exchange to the velocity endpoint of that URI, with the same options as this endpoint, which renders the text of a CamelVelocityTemplate header instead if one is set.

CamelVelocityTemplate.description: The text of a template that the producer renders in place of the template of resourceUri. Only used when allowTemplateFromHeader is true. The producer removes the header after reading it.

CamelVelocityContext.description: The org.apache.velocity.context.Context that the template reads its data from, in place of the context that the producer builds from the exchange with the body, the headers and the other entries. Only used when allowTemplateFromHeader is true. The CamelVelocitySupplementalContext header is then ignored.

CamelVelocitySupplementalContext.description: A Map of entries that the producer adds to the context that it builds from the exchange, where an entry replaces the one with the same key, such as body or headers. Only used when allowTemplateFromHeader is true, and not when the CamelVelocityContext header is set.

producerIn.description: The template gets the body as body, as it is: text, or a Map, a List or a POJO to read from; convert bytes or a stream to a String first. The template is the resource, or the CamelVelocityTemplate or CamelVelocityResourceUri header with allowTemplateFromHeader=true, and never the body

producerOut.description: The text the template writes, also when it is JSON or XML: unmarshal it to read its fields. The headers are kept

resourceUri.description: Path to the resource. You can prefix with: classpath, file, http, ref, or bean. classpath, file and http loads the resource using these protocols (classpath is default). ref will lookup the resource in the registry. bean will call a method on a bean to be used as the resource. For bean you can specify the method name after dot, eg bean:myBean.myMethod.

allowContextMapAll.description: Sets whether the context map should allow access to all details. By default only the message body and headers can be accessed. This option can be enabled for full access to the current Exchange and CamelContext. Doing so impose a potential security risk as this opens access to the full power of CamelContext API.

allowTemplateFromHeader.description: Whether the producer reads the CamelVelocityResourceUri, CamelVelocityTemplate, CamelVelocityContext and CamelVelocitySupplementalContext headers. If false, the producer ignores all four headers. Enable it only when the route sets these headers, not a message sender.

contentCache.description: Sets whether to use resource content cache or not

encoding.description: The name of the character encoding (charset) that the producer uses to read the template of resourceUri, for example UTF-8. If not set, the default charset of the JVM is used. Not used for the template of the CamelVelocityTemplate header, which is already text, nor for the templates that #parse or #include loads.

loaderCache.description: Whether the file resource loader of the VelocityEngine caches the templates that a template includes with #parse or #include. It does not apply to the template of resourceUri, which the producer reads itself and contentCache caches. Not used when the velocityEngine option of the component is set, and the propertiesFile can override it.

propertiesFile.description: The URI of a Java properties file with the configuration of the VelocityEngine that the endpoint creates, for example file:velocity.properties, or a path on the classpath when the URI has no scheme. Its properties replace the defaults that Camel sets, such as the resource loaders and loaderCache. Not used when the velocityEngine option of the component is set.
